findings.claim: The new early return in `CollectGeneric` skips every closed generic whose definition comes from metadata before its substituted members or type arguments are collected. On base, `GetObjectInfo` walked the substituted members of such types; per the requirement, `class Item<T>` was an "ok" row. Consider a lib `[MessagePackObject] class Item<T> { [Key(0)] public T Value; }` used in app as `Item<MyEnum>` or `Item<LocalNonRootType[]>`, where `MyEnum` is declared in app and reached only through that type argument. The app resolver would no longer register a formatter for `MyEnum`. Ledger L8 only exempts formatters for referenced types; `MyEnum` belongs to app. This would contradict "closed generic classes ... keep working as before" and leave trimmed/NativeAOT apps without the formatter at runtime.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a lib containing `[MessagePackObject] public class Item<T> { [Key(0)] public T Value { get; set; } }` to an image and reference it from app. App has `public enum MyEnum { A }` and `[MessagePackObject] public class Cmd { [Key(0)] public Item<MyEnum> M { get; set; } }`. Run MessagePackGenerator on base and on head and diff the generated resolver. Expect base to register a formatter for `MyEnum` and head to omit it.

findings.claim: `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wraps every TypeCollector diagnostic and silently drops any diagnostic with Location.None or a metadata location. This includes Error diagnostics (MsgPack004 is an Error per L2) about a `[MessagePackObject]` type declared in the current compilation, when the offending member is inherited from a base class in a referenced assembly. That base class may not be `[MessagePackObject]`, so no project ever reports the problem. This contradicts the new docs claim that such problems are reported by the defining project. The requirement asks only that these paths not crash. Roslyn allows reporting at Location.None, and a fallback location such as the derived type's identifier was available.

receipt_plan.detail: Lib: `public class Base { public int X { get; set; } }` (not MessagePackObject), emitted as a metadata reference. App: `[MessagePackObject] public class Derived : Base { [Key(0)] public int Y { get; set; } }`. Run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer on head. It reports no MsgPack004 for X, and the generator emits a formatter that silently omits X.
